title: The Donkey in Lion's Skin
summary: A foolish courtier dresses in royal silk and tries to terrify the council with fierce commands. Birbal demonstrates why true majesty is quiet.
full_text:
A cowardly but wealthy courtier named Mirza Jafar purchased a magnificent cape of gold-embroidered crimson silk and a towering turban pinned with a falcon feather. Hoping to inspire awe and fear among the junior clerks and servants, Jafar paced through the palace corridors, scowling fiercely and shouting harsh commands like an imperial conqueror.

Watching this absurd spectacle, Birbal turned to Emperor Akbar and said: 'Sire, Jafar reminds me of the ancient tale of the washerman's donkey who wore a lion's skin.'

Akbar asked: 'How did that story go, Birbal?'

Birbal narrated: 'In a village near the forest, an impoverished washerman found the dried carcass of a dead lion. He skinned the beast, dried the pelt, and draped it over his skinny, hungry donkey.

'At night, the washerman drove the donkey into the villagers' lush barley fields. The farmers, seeing the yellow maned figure in the moonlight, fled in terror, crying: "A man-eating lion is in our crops!"

'Night after night, the donkey feasted upon the tender grain, growing fat and sleek under the lion's skin.

'One moonlit night, while the donkey was grazing peacefully in the barley, a female donkey in a distant pasture brayed loudly: *Hee-haw! Hee-haw!*

'Hearing the call of his own kind, the foolish donkey forgot his royal lion pelt! He lifted his snout, puffed his chest, and brayed back with all his might: *HEE-HAW! HEE-HAW!*

'The farmers, hearing the ridiculous braying emerging from the "lion," stopped running. They grabbed heavy bamboo clubs, surrounded the field, and beat the pretender until he could barely limp away!'

Akbar roared with laughter. Birbal concluded: 'Sire, a man may wrap himself in the robes of kings and adopt the snarl of a warrior. But the moment he opens his mouth to speak, the true nature of his mind is laid bare for all the world to see.'

Mirza Jafar, who had overheard the story, hung his head in mortification, took off his flamboyant cape, and learned to behave with modest dignity.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Donkey in Lion's Skin"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
